questions.knowledge_point: Visualizing Intersections of Uncountable Families of Indexed Sets
questions.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[-1,1]\times [-i,i].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[-1,1]\times [-0.5,0.5]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [-1,1],b\in [-0.5,0.5]}.
$$

This represents a rectangle whose vertices are at $(1,-0.5),$ $(1,0.5),$ $(-1,0.5),$ and $(-1,-0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/f0a530434b8ac38fdb4cb517f22e121892c8b7c635c702c1cd9fccb2961aee18.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[-1,1]\times [-i,i]={(a,b)\,:\,a\in [-1,1],b\in [-i,i]}
$$

is the rectangle whose vertices are at $(1,-i),$ $(1,i),$ $(-1,i),$ and $(-1,-i).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/6982658bd8ce0e3c81953309ed9f2a70d1e56bbfce8af8862a32da66bf19e638.png)

 

The intersection of all these rectangles is the line segment $[-1,1]\times {0}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/34a3addbdcf3d5348805f494ed2e427f21f6ad424b0d9d2a411dae9f99b2fb7a.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Visualizing Unions of Uncountable Families of Indexed Sets
questions.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,i]\times {i}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the union of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *at least one* set:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for at least one}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=0.5,$ we have 

$$
{X}_{0.5}=[0,0.5]\times {0.5}={(k,0.5)\,:\,k\in [0,0.5]}.
$$

This represents a horizontal line segment from the point $(0,0.5)$ to the point $(0.5,0.5)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/7587daeaea45c5ef3449ecb676133c60bbedb7819308783bac835f3ae9c6883c.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}=[0,i]\times {i}={(k,i)\,:\,k\in [0,i]}
$$

is the horizontal line segment from the point $(0,i)$ to the point $(i,i).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/b926204a3d58b25889f1c79dd0f65c1ea990c67bc88e869004396a77970e8dd4.png)

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following triangle that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/4a81de1a698eedf6a636d66b68a7c62efa69d1d026a961ae97ab5ecc2ef9828d.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Sketching Cartesian Products of Special Sets in the Coordinate Plane
questions.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=N\times R$ in the Cartesian plane?
questions.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=N\times R
$$

 
contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is a natural number and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in N,\,y\in R}
$$

To visualize $S,$ consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{1}={(1,y)\,:\,y\in R}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/067b3b386273b09d5614f934f6525bd3e43ff46f420eb8aa7e744f635ff6d101.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number.

$$
{S}_{2}={(2,y)\,:\,y\in R}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{2}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/a870f65350ad00d258471079a34bec49a47d331c176dc7a91b3c7aae5ae968dd.png)

We can create the subsets ${S}_{3},{S}_{4},{S}_{5},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product consists of the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}R\times N & ={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}\cup {S}_{3}\cup … \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in N}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $R\times N$ as the set of vertical lines shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/c0df23ec47d729f597c02acff1530dd646a6f6c506a6497a8cb4d75b7fce5e74.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Sketching Cartesian Products of Special Sets in the Coordinate Plane
questions.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S={Z}^{-}\times {Z}^{-}$ in the Cartesian plane?
questions.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S={Z}^{-}\times {Z}^{-}
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is a negative integer and whose $y$-coordinate is a negative integer.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in {Z}^{-},\,y\in {Z}^{-}}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is negative integer.

$$
{S}_{-1}={(-1,y)\,:\,y\in {Z}^{-}}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/37ad5627c3fb7cc89e751bb697e01ac7fecaf2712e230b6e3812ad9137d5cd46.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{-2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any negative integer.

$$
{S}_{-2}={(-2,y)\,:\,y\in {Z}^{-}}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-2}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/97ebcac85477b8e88564ab67d59c926d5faa72138c8a31d80d3b89895f33668c.png)

We can create the subsets $…{S}_{-5},{S}_{-4},{S}_{-3}$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =…{S}_{-5}\cup {S}_{-4}\cup {S}_{-3}\cup {S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1} \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in {Z}^{-}}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize ${Z}^{-}\times {Z}^{-}$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/a756e53554cb9184d96a52b83038fbd6b00b21d0a12cc658aebb5010e917fd03.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Visualizing Unions of Uncountable Families of Indexed Sets
questions.problem: Which of the following represents the set $S=[-1,1]\times [0,1]$ in the Cartesian plane?
questions.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set

$$
S=[-1,1]\times [0,1]
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in [-1,1],\,y\in [0,1]}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{0}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $0$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
{S}_{0}={(0,y)\,:\,y\in [0,1]}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{0}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/1cc30fcc7543bfbbf8c5c59d1436eb3b1a0799d60c9ad1d899957e8fd17d58ab.png)

Now, consider a general ${S}_{i}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals some $i\in [-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
{S}_{i}={(i,y)\,:\,y\in [0,1]}
$$

For each $i\in [-1,1],$ ${S}_{i}$ is a vertical line segment from the point $(i,0)$ to the point $(i,1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/494c9d77b0ff339b90792270c9d641054a03a2918e3c56a93747b42a77ee3ccf.png)

Our Cartesian product $S$ is the union of these subsets over $I=[-1,1]:$

$$
S={⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i}.
$$

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following rectangle that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044579/assets/7c5ac5dad0aaacb4347c260d634e6bcd2d6102b25d51813fe106803417cc7539.png)
